projects.flagshipProject: Trellis, Bellwether and Quarry - internal model promotion, monitoring and shared features
projects.description: AWS runs machine learning inside its own services long before any of it becomes a product, and the teams doing it sit all over the company - fraud, support routing, capacity forecasting, retail-facing tooling - none of whom want to build the same plumbing twice. A practitioner trains a model in Slipway, the hosted workspace; it is registered and reviewed in Trellis before it may answer real requests; Quarry supplies the shared features so two teams computing the same signal agree; Wayfinder sizes what serves it and how much is shared; and Bellwether measures what production actually sends against what the model learned from, with the Model Risk Review board signing off anything customer-facing. Modelling comes first here - training, fine-tuning, forecasting, outlier detection, retrieval assistants, controlled experiments, evaluation and drift detection - resting on a data estate of streaming and batch pipelines, shared features, datasets and usage analytics; served by cloud training, inference and event orchestration; exposed through the console teams work in and the APIs their own products call; scheduled against shared capacity with isolation and observability; and fenced by tenant separation, provenance, explainability review and the FedRAMP evidence a government-facing service needs.

projects.flagshipProject: Claims scoring, fraud detection and catastrophe-response analytics
projects.description: USAA serves military members and their families with banking, insurance and investments. Claims and fraud are where machine learning earns its place: a claim arrives and has to be triaged and routed, and a payment or login has to be judged before it completes, both inside a regulated workflow where every automated decision has to be explainable to an actuary or an examiner.
bullets: Delivered the claims-scoring services at USAA, triaging incoming auto and property claims by severity and routing them so straightforward losses settled without an adjuster ever opening the file.

Developed fraud and account-takeover detection across member servicing and payments, weighing behavioural history against device and session signals to raise activity for review rather than blocking a member outright.
Stood up the training and feature pipelines those models ran on, replacing hand-cut extracts of claims, policy, payment and contact history with a reproducible build an examiner could follow.
Ranked exposure and dispatch priority after hurricanes and hailstorms, giving claims operations a defensible order of work in the weeks when volume arrived faster than adjusters could be assigned.
Sat with actuarial, compliance and claims leadership through model reviews, and wrote up what each score was entitled to decide, which is the reason any of it was allowed near underwriting.

projects.flagshipProject: Payments risk, identity verification and transaction monitoring
projects.description: Coinbase is a retail crypto exchange, and in this period its problem was growth: onboarding, funding and withdrawal all had to be judged in real time while volume grew faster than the systems behind them were designed for. Risk scoring, identity verification and transaction monitoring were the models that decided whether a customer got through in seconds or waited for a human.
bullets: Built risk and fraud scoring for deposits, withdrawals and card funding at Coinbase, separating genuine new customers from chargeback and stolen-instrument attempts at the point of transaction.

Developed identity-verification and onboarding models that decided which applications could clear automatically and which needed manual review, keeping compliance obligations met without stalling legitimate signups.
Engineered transaction-monitoring pipelines over on-chain and internal ledger activity, surfacing patterns that mattered to anti-money-laundering review instead of alerting on raw volume.
Rebuilt the batch and streaming data paths behind those models when trading volume grew far faster than the original design assumed, moving scoring off overnight jobs and onto the request path.
